High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1. Due to call given by High Court Bar Association, Gwalior, lawyers are abstaining from work.

2. The present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashment of the FIR dated 06-11-2012 registered at Police Station Bahodapur District Gwalior at Crime No.526/2012 for offence under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 419 of IPC on the basis of compromise.
3. At the outset, respondent No.2 - Mohd. Kamaruddin (Ahar No.463808443386) submits that both the parties settled the matter and entered into compromise.
Respondent No.2 is complainant and his wife Smt. Rabiya Bano (Adhar No.807681669649) and sister-in-law Smt. Nargis (Adhar No.867188565919) were the persons aggrieved.

During pendency of trial bearing No.150/2021 ST (pending before VIII Additional Sessions Judge,Gwalior), compromise reached between the parties,
therefore, applications vide I.A.No.21651/2024 and I.A. No.21652/2024 have been preferred at the instance of parties and they want to settle the matter.
Applications are duly signed by respective parties and same are supported by their affidavits.

sentences.text: In pursuance to the order dated 01-04-2025, the Principal Registrar of this Court has duly verified the parties, contents of application, intent and signatures of parties.
At the time of preparation of verification report petitioner - Shravan Kumar also appeared before Principal Registrar of this Court on 09-04-2025 and showed his intention for settlement.
Now purpose of lodging the FIR against petitioner is over because complainant and aggrieved persons received required payment.

5. Heard.
6.
A Lean Compromise is better than a Fat Law Suit , instant efforts of the parties indicate the same.
It is expected that their bona fide gestures would continue.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of judgments Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another, AIR 2008 SC 1968, Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 2008 SC 1969, Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another, (2011) 10 SCC 705, Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675, Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Parbatbhai Ahir alias Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another, (2017) 9 SCC 641 , laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.
8.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into account the law laid down by the Apex Court, in the opinion of this Court, continuance of trial in such matter will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Further parties have settled the matter and decided to finalize the dispute inter se.
Under such a situation, Section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.

9. Thus, in the interest of justice, application for compounding the offence vide I.A.No.21651/2024 and I.A. No.21652/2024 are allowed because no fruitful purpose would be served in continuation of trial.
Thus, parties are permitted to compound the offences.
10. Resultantly, the petition is allowed.

FIR dated 06-11-2012 registered at Police Station Bahodapur District Gwalior at Crime No.526/2012 for offence under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 419 of IPC are hereby quashed against the petitioner on the basis of compromise.
Petitioner is discharged from all the charges.
11. Petition stands allowed and disposed of in above terms.
12. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
13. Certified copy as per rules.

(ANAND PATHAK) (DR. S.K. MATHUR)
